rationale: Round 1 built cleanly and passed correctness with no ICE fallback, so round 2 escalates obfuscation aggressiveness across all seven passes. This target is a small C++ expression-derivation program whose value is concentrated in a handful of medium functions (main at 558 bytes, quotient_expr::deriv at 399 bytes) built around a class hierarchy with virtual-style deriv/print methods, so the table prioritizes control-flow flattening (FLA) and bogus control flow (BCF) to destroy the recognizable recursive-derivative structure of the deriv methods, with instruction substitution (SUB) and indirect branch (IBR) raised to complement them and erase basic-block fingerprints left by flattening. ICALL and IGV are kept in the mix at moderate security weight because indirect calls and global variable obfuscation disrupt the class-hierarchy symbol/vtable patterns that make this program easy to annotate in a decompiler, while their slightly higher correctness weights reflect the greater fragility of rewriting call targets and global references in C++ code. Cost dimensions are deliberately kept below the security/diversity gains because the program is tiny (1720 total text bytes, 16 functions) and its runtime is dominated by trivial arithmetic, meaning even multi-x overhead from BCF/FLA stays well within acceptable bounds; the modest bump of BCF/FLA SizeCost and RuntimeCost versus round 1 simply encodes their true relative expense so they concentrate on the largest, most valuable functions instead of the many trivial ones.
